summary: `verification.result` in a task record is an enum of exactly three values — `not-run`, `pass`, `fail` — and there is no word for a run that verified part of a change. That is not a documentation gap; it is the mechanism by which a lane records a false pass. A lane that ran half its tier and knows it cannot honestly write `pass` has exactly two schema-legal answers, and one of them is a lie.
why_this_is_not_a_nitpick: CP-120's whole argument is that lanes will record `pass` for a run that did not cover the change, and that such a recording is unrecoverable once it is in a task record. RELEASE-011 closed the tier's half of that: the feature tier now refuses to print `pass` and refuses to exit 0 when a step did not run. But the tier now emits a verdict (`incomplete`) that a task record CANNOT EXPRESS, so the pressure CP-120 identified has simply moved from the tier to the record. RELEASE-010 is the worked example in this repository: its record carries `result: "pass"` and a summary stating that the tier itself returned a truthful red. The record was honest in its prose and false in its field, and a reader taking the field is misled. A schema that cannot say `partial` will be filled in with whichever of the other two words is less embarrassing.

the_change.IMPORTANT: docs/engineering/tasks/task.schema.json is GENERATED — control-plane.mjs:708 writes it from `taskSchema()`. Editing the JSON alone would be silently reverted by `npm run agents:generate`. The generator is the only place that has to change.
the_change.why_not_applied_here: scripts/agent-tools/** is the control plane's own machinery, shared by every agent's validation, and a concurrent lane is regenerating the maps. RELEASE-011 routed it instead of taking it, which is the same rule CP-112 and CP-101 applied to grants.

suggested_meaning_of_partial: `partial` = the recorded tier reported `incomplete`: nothing that ran failed, and the record names the skipped checks. It is a claim about coverage, not about correctness, and it is strictly more informative than `not-run`, which means nothing ran at all. If the orchestrator prefers a different word (`inconclusive`, `coverage-partial`), the only requirement is that it exists and that DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md and the tier's `RESULT:` vocabulary use the same one.
what_release_011_did_in_the_meantime: The feature tier already refuses to print `RESULT: pass` and refuses to exit 0 when a step did not run, so no lane can obtain a green tier by accident regardless of the schema.
`docs/DEVELOPMENT_WORKFLOW.md` tells lanes to record `partial` with the named skipped set, so the vocabulary is already in the instructions even though the schema does not yet accept it.
This is the one RELEASE-011 acceptance criterion-adjacent item that could not be closed inside its own grant, and it is recorded rather than left implicit.
next_steps: Orchestrator: add 'partial' to the two lists in control-plane.mjs, run npm run agents:generate, and confirm agents:validate accepts a record carrying it.
Optional and separable: a `verification.skipped` array of {check, missing} so a partial record carries its reason structurally rather than in prose. Not required for the fix.
